title: Python: R4, a local whose every binding is Cls(...) of one class resolves its method calls (DEC-303 (a22) item 3)
description: DEC-303 (a22) item 3, group R4, verbatim: 'R4, every binding of a local is Cls(...) of one class: admitted under item 2, with the nonlocal proviso.' Governing line (a22) item 2: a target is admitted when EVERY binding of the name can be enumerated from the text of its scope; for a local, writes through nonlocal in nested scopes count as bindings. Second in the DEC-303 (a23) build order after M1 (R4, ALIAS, TS, Q1, (a25), NB-b, step 5) that releases the (a36) hold on the fresh blind sample. Per (a23) item 1 the item-3 group sizes are re-derived on the fixed baseline. Interaction with (a25) (a later task): a write to x.m on a local x bound under R4 or E1 makes x.m() unresolved; not built here. Lessons from K1, LIT and M1 to apply before the first push: enumerate every way the name can get a second binding in EVERY module the rule reads (the scope, any nested scope through nonlocal, and any module a constructor import passes through), give each its own refused fixture asserting no edge leaves the call site and the receiver bin, count bindings with enumerableBindings (never S3 localNames), refuse module-level stars, and read stars, globals, class bodies and annotations. Existing 6d knownClassOf and E1 resolve an imported or dotted constructor by qualname with source-module bindings uncounted (named follow-up; R4 must not widen that gap).

acceptanceCriteria.text: a local whose EVERY binding in its scope is a call Cls(...) of one and the same in-repo class (two or more such bindings allowed, nothing else) resolves a method call on it to that class method, with red-before fixtures and positive and negative twins; the class must pass the same checks as the 6d known-class local case and E1 (MRO ok, no __new__, no metaclass, no opaque base, no replacing decorator)

each of these leaves the call unresolved, each with its own refused fixture asserting no edge leaves the call site and the call stays in its current bin (bin delta against the same file without the rule): any binding of the local that is not Cls(...) of that class (a different class, a factory, a literal, a parameter, for, with-as, except-as, walrus, comprehension target, match capture, import, def, class, augmented, annotated, tuple or star target, type alias); an enumerated binding that cannot be read; a nonlocal write from a nested scope (def or lambda, at any depth) that binds the name to anything but Cls(...) of the same class, and a nonlocal binding in a nested scope counted as a binding of the local; a global declaration of the name in the scope; a class-body binding of the name (a read from a class body or a comprehension inside the function sees the local and resolves, with fixtures, round 1 F5); a constructor that is a dotted name, an imported name whose source module has a second binding, a factory, an external class; all bindings counting through the shared enumeration (enumerableBindings), never S3 localNames

each rule has a mutation check that goes red (mutants listed by name, equivalent mutants said so), and a per-site corpus diff on the five pins is recorded, with every in-repo edge it creates or removes named per site and sent to the leader before the clear; no receiver-to-external moves unexplained

implementationNotes: Built (DEC-303 (a22) item 3, R4). PROBE: before the change a local with two or more `x = C()` bindings (single is rule 6d's) was receiver-needs-inference. BUILT in src/python/calls.ts: localConstructedClass, called from resolveAttributeCall after the 6d known-class step, one segment only. The name is found in a function or lambda scope (a module-level or class-body name is not R4); its bindings come from enumerableBindings (global declaration between use and local, class-body, star refuse); EVERY binding must be an unannotated assign whose right-hand side is a call with a BARE-NAME callee (a dotted callee Outer.Inner(), k.C() refuses); each constructor name is resolved by classSymbolOfName (generalised from moduleClassSymbol, which now wraps it): exactly ONE binding by enumerableBindings, a class statement, or a direct from-import of a module file whose own binding of the name is one class (re-export hop, package __init__, conditional import, a second binding or star in the source module all refuse); all bindings must name the SAME class symbol, which must pass instanceClassOf (ok MRO, no __new__, no metaclass, no opaque base, no replacing decorator). Writes through nonlocal in nested scopes are in the binding list (applyScopeRedirects); a new RawBinding.origin records the scope whose text holds a nonlocal-moved binding so its constructor name is read there (a shadowing local C or def C in the nested scope refuses). Lesson applied: every refusal fixture asserts no edge to .run leaves the call site and that the call is exactly one receiver-needs-inference site more than the same source with the call replaced by pass. FIXTURES (test/python-calls.test.ts, describe R4, 8 tests): positives (two or three bindings, closure read, nonlocal one and two levels, subclass inheriting, imported constructor, alias); 25 second-binding forms (different class, None, literal, factory, alias, augmented, for, with-as, except-as, walrus, comprehension target, match capture, tuple, starred, list, import, from-import, def, class, annotated, bare annotation, type alias, dotted constructor, call of a call, global declaration); parameter, default, splat; nonlocal writes of another class, literal, augmented, for, import, rebound or def constructor in the nested scope, global declaration in a nested function; constructor name with two classes, rebind, call rebind, for, with-as, walrus, global write from function and class body, star, local alias; imported constructor with a second binding, second class, for, walrus, with-as, global write, star in its source module, re-export hop, package __init__, hop whose re-exporting module rebinds or has a for, conditional import, two imports, dotted module constructor; class checks (__new__, metaclass, opaque base, replacing decorator, external class, def named like a class); module-level and class-body names stay refused; multi-segment and call of the local not widened. RED BEFORE: with the hook off the positive fixtures fail. MUTANTS (replace-text, each run with bun test test/python-calls.test.ts -t R4), 12 RED: hook-off, scope-kind (function or lambda only), enumerable (enumerableBindings to lookupBindings), annotation, rhs-call, callee-name (bare name), origin (binding.origin to found scope), ctor-count, ctor-enumerable, same-class, instance-class (instanceClassOf), origin-nonlocal. Three mutants SURVIVED on the first draft and the checks were REMOVED as redundant: the length >= 2 test (a single binding is 6d's, which runs first and refuses a superset; equivalent), the binding.kind === assign test (only an assign carries an rhs), and origin on the global redirect (found scope must be a function, so a global-moved binding is never in the list); a missing fixture for a global declaration in a nested function was added for the enumerableBindings mutant. ROUND 1 FIXES (review of 97961815). B1: a comprehension target is recorded by the walker as a binding of the enclosing function, and applyScopeRedirects sent a nonlocal write to the nearest function where bindings.has(name), so a comprehension over the name in an intermediate function captured the write (R4 resolved x.run to C.run while x was D at runtime). Fixed in the shared walker: RawBinding.comprehension marks for_in_clause targets, and the nonlocal target search ignores a scope whose only bindings of the name are comprehension targets (the binding stays counted, so a read still refuses; Python binds it in the comprehension's own scope). The same fix covers a constructor NAME. Fixtures: list, generator, set, dict comprehension, tuple target, a comprehension in a default argument, a constructor name behind a comprehension, plus a twin over another name. F1: fixture for the two-level nonlocal write whose constructor is rebound in the innermost scope kills the origin ??= to = mutant. F2: comment corrected. F3: the lambda arm of the scope-kind test dropped (a lambda holds only parameters, so it was unreachable). F4: the invalid assign-then-global fixture replaced by a valid global-first fixture. F5: AC2 reworded (the words were mine, not the DEC text): a read from a class body or comprehension inside the function sees the local and resolves, fixtured both ways, and a class-body binding of the name refuses. F6: no case named, no action. MUTANTS now 15 RED, adding comp-flag (has instead of the comprehension-aware search), comp-mark and origin-first. CORPUS DIFF re-run on the five pins against origin/dev 62cf448: IDENTICAL to round 0, the same 54 receiver-needs-inference to in-repo edges and nothing else, so the walker change moves no site of rule 6d, K1, LIT, M1 or any other rule on these corpora (the diff would assert any receiver-to-external move).

ROUND 2 (review of d606754, nothing blocking; test and comment only push). N1: the edge half of the R4 refused() helper filtered calleeId.endsWith('.run') but a calleeId is a symbol id (file:row:col), so it never matched; it now compares against the symbol ids of every run method in the fixture. Confirmed by mutation with the bin half of the helper disabled: dropping the same-class check and dropping the annotation check each turn the edge half RED on a real edge (calleeId app.py:6:9). N2: a 6d twin and a LIT twin of the B1 comprehension fixture. N3: the comment on the scope-kind test says what a lambda can hold (a walrus or a comprehension target, neither an assign with a call right-hand side, so the lambda arm is behaviour-equivalent); this is the only src/ line changed and it is a comment. N4: async, parenthesized and nested comprehension targets, and the positive walrus-in-comprehension twin (a walrus binds in g, where the nonlocal write lands, so f's local stays C and x.run() resolves). N5 (PEP 695 type parameters bind no name, so def h[x](): x.run() resolves to C.run) is pre-existing and shared with 6d: filed as a follow-up, not fixed here. No behaviour change: the five-pin corpus diff is unchanged because no code changed.
